headline: Withheld and independent validation reshape how biological prediction models are judged
label: Validation Design In Computational Biology
summary: Benchmark accuracy alone no longer suffices; recent preprints test transfer, baselines and retrieval against withheld or independent data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is supervised or self-supervised models whose outputs are checked against withheld or independent data. Several items test whether performance survives validation: a frozen cross-context perturbation model is scored on the public 2025 Virtual Cell Challenge benchmark, a baseline-aware framework asks whether sequence models add value in noncoding RNA assays, and degree-matched AUROC is separated from screen retrieval in synthetic-lethality prediction. Reliability is treated as distinct from prediction: SHAP-based reliability-attribution fingerprints indicate that reliability transfer in single-cell foundation models does not follow prediction transfer. Source selection is examined by asking whether transcriptomic similarity ranks contexts beyond tissue matching. The Tclin-likeness model uses temporally withheld validation. What is new is the emphasis on validation design rather than benchmark claims alone; the excerpts report no accuracy figures for the biomarker and pathway studies, so predictive validity is not established here.
